title: Rethinking Structured Generation: Can Graph-Based Reasoning Resolve Ambiguity?
abstract: arXiv:2610.31681v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Structured generation is typically formulated as a deterministic mapping from input to a single structured output. This assumption is fundamentally misaligned with natural language, which often admits multiple structurally distinct yet semantically valid interpretations. As a result, existing methods rely on single-reference supervision that collapses ambiguity into one prediction, leading to unstable and inconsistent outputs under underspecified inputs. We reformulate structured generation as an \textit{ambiguity-aware inference problem}, where the objective is to reason over a set of plausible structured outputs rather than predict a single solution. We show that standard training inherently suppresses valid alternatives, and instead adopt a multi-valid learning framework that preserves ambiguity during optimization. translated_title: 重新思考结构化生成：基于图的推理能否解决歧义问题？
translated_abstract: 结构化生成通常被表述为从输入到单一结构化输出的确定性映射。这一假设与自然语言存在根本性的不匹配，因为自然语言往往允许多种结构上不同但语义上均有效的解释。因此，现有方法依赖于单一参考监督，将歧义压缩为单一预测，导致在欠指定输入下产生不稳定且不一致的输出。我们将结构化生成重新表述为一个歧义感知推理问题，其目标是对一组合理的结构化输出进行推理，而非预测单一解。我们证明标准训练本质上会抑制有效的替代方案，因此我们采用了一种多有效学习框架，在优化过程中保留歧义。为了将这一表述付诸实践，我们构建了一个结构化输出的候选空间，将每个候选表示为……
tldr: 该论文将结构化生成重新表述为歧义感知推理问题，提出基于图推理的多有效学习框架，通过对一组合理的结构化输出进行推理而非预测单一解，解决了自然语言歧义导致现有方法输出不稳定和不一致的问题。
